title: The Rule That Stops at the Fence
concept: On October 20th the Kenai Peninsula Borough Assembly passed a weather modification rule after California's Rainmaker flew a cloud seeding drone near Homer. The rule is a form that attaches to borough land only. The film draws the form as Dotty, a paper character who is pinned to the borough's own ground and asks four things about a flight, beside a rain gauge, while the sky above belongs to the FAA and the state office is dark and empty. It gives the fair case a scene (a land permit was never going to measure the weather, both sides are quoted, the assembly has asked the Legislature) and ends on one fact: the form asks what a flight intends, the gauge carries only Rainmaker's tag, and the reports found describe no outside check of the rain Rainmaker says it made.

fingerprint.palette: first-snow white and mist-blue, a paper form hero with checkbox eyes, emerald borough ground, indigo and plum upper floors, a late summer viridian and gold bay, a single amber tag on the rain gauge's second hook, a black tack
fingerprint.camera_strategy: pull-backs from a desk to a three floor building, a tilted parcel plane, a dive into a hairline and a craneDown through the floors
fingerprint.light_story: an overcast first-snow day, a lit ground floor under two dark floors, a late summer gold bay in flashback, a cool snow window wall with no lamp, cold grey blinds in an empty state office, then flat noon light on a rain gauge in the snow
fingerprint.metaphor: a form that can only be pinned to the ground it stands on, beside a rain gauge with a hook nobody has hung an outside reading on

palette: first-snow white and mist-blue, a paper form hero with checkbox eyes, emerald borough ground, indigo and plum upper floors, a late summer viridian and gold bay, a single amber tag on the rain gauge's second hook, a black tack
divergence_note: 10-22 was a dusk tundra survey table in spruce ink, brass and vermilion with a plumb bob. 10-21 was a pewter beach with a tawny calf. 10-20 was a celadon and walnut office with a manila folder and a lamp. This film is a bright first-snow day with a paper form hero, an emerald borough accent, indigo and plum floors, a late summer viridian and gold flashback and an amber hook tag, and it moves through a snowy three floor building cutaway, a tilted parcel plane, a summer bay map, a forecast panel, an empty state office and a rain gauge in the snow. HONEST OVERLAP: a paper document hero with a face, as in 10-20, and a question that ends on an absence, as in 10-22.

treatment.winner: The Explainer's three floor building and the dive into 19 million gallons being a hairline, with the Comedian's characterized form (Dotty) as hero, a rain gauge with an empty hook as the throughline object, the Dramatist's conditional Vance bill, and the Enthusiast's fair-case template scene.
treatment.why: A form with a face carries the thesis in one image (it can only be pinned to the ground it stands on), the lit floor under two dark ones makes jurisdiction a picture a muted viewer can read, and a rain gauge with a bare hook gives a planted promise that pays at the button.

angle.thesis: A borough can only write a rule for the ground a drone takes off from, so Kenai's new permit collects what an operator intends to do, while the only number anyone has for what came out of the sky is the company's own.
angle.falsifiable_by: An outside measurement of the August 23rd result (NWS, a university) turning up, or the rule turning out to require a measured post-flight result, or a state or federal rule turning out to already cover cloud seeding in Alaska.
supporting_facts: c2/c10/c11 the rule attaches to borough land (lease or land use permit); the mayor says reach is limited to borough lands and the FAA controls the skies
c9 DNR says state law doesn't address cloud seeding, so the middle layer is blank
c3 the application asks for intended outcome, chemicals, flares, flight frequency and duration
c6/c7/c15/c16 every output figure is Rainmaker's own, checked by its own method, and the reports don't describe an outside check
angle.counterpoint_honored: A land rule was never meant to be atmospheric science. The borough did what it could with the lever it has, said so plainly, and asked the Legislature for the rest (c13, c14). Rainmaker says it had every permission it needed and concedes more outreach was possible (c12); no harm is reported. A disclosure form is a template the state can copy. The film gives this its own scene at full strength, then lets the thesis narrow rather than break: the form asks for a prediction, nobody is yet set up to ask for the measurement.
angle.second_movement: The form is half a test: it puts a prediction on file. The picture is a form with its INTENDED OUTCOME slot filled and an outside-check slot that reads NOT REPORTED. The fact that recontextualises the first: the ground floor wrote the first draft because the floors above it are empty or federal.
angle.throughline_object: the application form (states: blank, filled with intended outcome, pinned to the borough parcel, a second slot for an outside check left dashed, final: the dashed slot is the question)
angle.ai_link_wording: A drone plus a forecasting platform, Stratus, that Rainmaker describes as taking in real time weather data to pick seeding windows. No source says AI, machine learning or autonomous. The film says drone and software, never AI.
angle.valence: even-handed, constructive about the borough's tool and Rainmaker's capability, skeptical only of the evidence chain; nobody a villain

runner_ups.SKEPTIC: 19 million gallons is a hundred: grafted as the second movement and the button
